nodes.label: AI Story Gen Drawer
nodes.rationale: Centralizes the scattered AI flow (ClipBin analyze + floating StoryBar + Inspector refine) into one slide-over drawer so steering, analysis, authoring and per-beat refine live in one place instead of three surfaces.

nodes.label: Script Type genre steer
nodes.rationale: A genre axis (product review / vlog / explainer / dramatic news / sports) deliberately kept orthogonal to Tone, so voice and genre compose rather than collapse into one preset list.

nodes.label: Deletion test
nodes.rationale: A module earns its keep only if deleting it would make complexity reappear across N callers; if complexity simply vanishes it was a pass-through. Vocabulary: module / interface / depth / seam / adapter / leverage / locality.

nodes.label: Candidate A — segment graph seam
nodes.rationale: Taken up first because the export filtergraph is unobservable, which blocks testing every other export-side change.

nodes.label: Candidate B — Frame module (preview/export parity by construction)
nodes.rationale: 16 visual properties are computed twice by two expressions that merely agree. Proposal: a Frame module returning the complete visual description of a Beat at time t as data, with the CSS and ffmpeg emitters as adapters that compute no geometry. Depends on Candidate A because the export half cannot be tested while the filtergraph is unobservable.

nodes.label: Candidate C — no component test harness
nodes.rationale: Zero .test.tsx files and vitest environment 'node' create a gravity well: testable logic migrates to util.ts and everything else stays stranded in Inspector.tsx (1968 lines). Add jsdom + testing-library first, then extract entity cards and one SliderRow.

nodes.label: Candidate D — four identical CRUD families in the Cut reducer
nodes.rationale: Weakest candidate: the reducer is already well tested, the duplication is stable rather than churning, and generic reducer factories trade readable repetition for unreadable abstraction.

nodes.label: Candidate E — util.ts is a shared-maths drawer
nodes.rationale: Fails the deletion test on its own — splitting a drawer into three drawers moves complexity rather than concentrating it. Only worth doing once a Frame module gives the framing half somewhere to go.

nodes.label: One module, two emitters rule
nodes.rationale: ADR-0008, ADR-0010 and ADR-0015 each declare the rule and each implements it separately for its own property, so no module owns 'what this Beat looks like at time t'. The pattern has already failed three times.

nodes.label: Overlay contain-vs-cover preview defect
nodes.rationale: Previews used objectFit cover while the export pads with fully transparent black — genuinely different pictures. Previews were moved to contain to match the export, because changing the export to fill would alter the output of existing projects. Whether cover is what authors actually want for grain/light-leak overlays is left open as a product decision.

nodes.label: Ken Burns time base — corrected over-claim
nodes.rationale: Not a live defect: setTrim holds durationSec equal to outSec−inSec on every editing path. What remains true is three expressions for one quantity agreeing by coincidence rather than by construction.

nodes.label: beatRotationStyle / beatZoomStyle split
nodes.rationale: Rotation and zoom were separated into two independent stages because CSS rotates about transform-origin (set to the zoom focus) while ffmpeg's rotate always rotates about the frame centre — with an off-centre focus the two disagreed on the pivot.

nodes.label: Export rotation sign inversion
nodes.rationale: rotationChain negated the angle on the false assumption that ffmpeg's rotate turns counter-clockwise for a positive value. Both ffmpeg rotate and CSS rotate() turn clockwise, so the negation was the inversion. Diagnosis cost time through console.debug being hidden, frame sampling every 2s stepping over a ~1.5s beat, and treating 'the frames changed' as proof of correctness.

nodes.label: Auto-cover for rotated frames
nodes.rationale: A rotated frame exposes triangular corners, so the effective scale is max(zoom, coverScale(θ)) and rotation punches in on its own — 3.1% at 1°, 15.1% at 5°, 42.6% at 15° on 16:9 because the height constraint dominates a wide frame.

nodes.label: gradeBeatToLook
nodes.rationale: The only function that accounts for where a shot already sits; analyzeFilmLook asks Claude for values that move NEUTRAL footage toward the look, so applying them flat to non-neutral footage overshoots.

nodes.label: Two-axis split-tone ColorAdjustments
nodes.rationale: tint, shadowWarmth/shadowTint and highlightWarmth/highlightTint were added first because cinematic looks are not representable without split-tone.

nodes.label: colorPalette.ts (global palette store)
nodes.rationale: Appends rather than reorders because a palette that moves under the cursor is worse than a stale one; rolling MAX_PALETTE of 20 drops from the front; subscribe() keeps every mounted picker live.

nodes.label: ColorField component
nodes.rationale: value/onChange only — it does not know what it is colouring, so one component can back Title layers, Sticker tint and anything later.

nodes.label: normalizeHex
nodes.rationale: The one place hex is canonicalised. Gained a typeof guard because it used to coerce, so a numeric 123 parsed as shorthand #112233 and would have put a colour nobody picked into the palette.

nodes.label: Binding constraint: no second palette
nodes.rationale: TITLE_SWATCHES and the Sticker tint row's inline list both had to go — one source of colours and one component that renders it, or the two lists drift.

nodes.label: curveStep
nodes.rationale: Exposure multiplicative, contrast pivoted at 0.5, split-tone weighted by tonal position — multiplicative exposure keeps black black, unlike the old additive eq=brightness export.

nodes.label: gradePixel(adj, rgb)
nodes.rationale: The reference every emitter derives from.

nodes.label: gradeSvgFilter (preview emitter)
nodes.rationale: Data-URI SVG with feComponentTransfer + feColorMatrix, pinning color-interpolation-filters=sRGB because SVG filters default to linearRGB and would diverge from the .cube bake.

nodes.label: gradeCube (.cube export emitter)
nodes.rationale: 33³ lattice straight from gradePixel; the drift guard compares the SVG path against gradePixel within one table interpolation interval.

nodes.label: ffmpegColorLut
nodes.rationale: Returns the EngineInput and the -vf entry together so they can never be added apart; replaced the eq/hue/colorbalance builder.

nodes.label: lookApply.ts (grade snapshot/restore)
nodes.rationale: Applying a Look clears the global fine-tune before writing per-Beat Grades (killing the double-apply); the snapshot carries the global override so Undo restores both.

nodes.label: Soft highlight shoulder
nodes.rationale: A tanh shoulder above a knee keeps overshooting values separated instead of all becoming 255; shadows keep a hard floor because black must stay black. Gated on curveOvershoots() so non-overshooting Grades keep both ends exact. Known limit: SVG clamps between filter primitives, so headroom cannot be carried through feColorMatrix without breaking parity with the LUT.

nodes.label: Shadows and Highlights luminance axes
nodes.rationale: Weights x(1-x)³ and (1-x)x³ peak at x=0.25 and x=0.75 and are zero at both ends, matching what Lightroom means by the words and therefore what Claude assumes when it emits a value. They live in curveStep so parity holds by construction.

nodes.label: Still
nodes.rationale: Has no natural length, so ingest gives it a synthetic 10-second duration and every consumer treats it as a 10-second source.

nodes.label: Direction
nodes.rationale: The editor is a curator by default; Direction makes it a collaborator. Shapes WHAT the Story says, where Tone shapes HOW it sounds.

nodes.label: Clip Description
nodes.rationale: A neutral description of the footage, never coaching aimed at the creator — the primary signal the Story is built from, since clips are not assumed to contain speech.

nodes.label: Overlay (B-roll)
nodes.rationale: Unlike a Beat it does not advance the Cut — it plays on top of whatever Beats it spans. Its blend mode is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Sticker
nodes.rationale: The asset comes from the author's stickers/ folder; the PLACEMENT is what lives in the Cut, so one asset can be placed many times.

nodes.label: Voiceover
nodes.rationale: When on, its length is the master clock for a Beat's on-screen duration.

nodes.label: Look
nodes.rationale: A Look is a TARGET the Beats are carried toward, not an offset added on top of them. Saving one under a name is all a 'preset' is.

nodes.label: Grade
nodes.rationale: Each Beat gets its own Grade because clips shot differently need different corrections to land in the same place. Three groups: overall, tonal range (Shadows/Highlights) and split tone.

nodes.label: Beat
nodes.rationale: The atomic story-and-edit unit: a Clip trimmed to in/out paired with the Script segment shown over it. A Clip appears in at most one Beat; Beats are not split or reused in v1.

nodes.label: Layer
nodes.rationale: Something laid OVER a Beat's picture rather than being it. Zoom, Ken Burns, rotation and the Grade are deliberately NOT Layers — they decide what the shot itself looks like.

nodes.label: Ken Burns (moving framing)
nodes.rationale: It exists because a Still has nothing else to give the eye — the picture does not change, so the framing must. A Beat's framing is either a Zoom or a Ken Burns, never both, because the two command the same thing.

nodes.label: ADR-0004 — Voiceover length as master clock
ADR-0008 — Shared canvas renderer for text
nodes.rationale: One renderer feeds both the preview and the export so text geometry cannot drift between them.

nodes.label: CSS design tokens (dark/light theme)
nodes.rationale: Never hardcode arbitrary hex/RGB or native browser defaults; all colour flows through custom properties in studio.css so both themes stay coherent and design does not drift.

nodes.label: Switch component
nodes.rationale: Switch rules are prefixed with .studio so they win over the global .studio button reset.

nodes.label: SVG close-affordance rule
nodes.rationale: Every modal/drawer close affordance renders an x SVG icon, never a unicode character or 'Close' text, always with aria-label and Esc wired.

nodes.label: Pointer-event propagation in draggable containers
nodes.rationale: Parent containers invoke setPointerCapture on onPointerDown, so stopping propagation only on click lets the parent drag handler hijack pointer capture before the button's click can fire.

nodes.label: runIsolated (one isolated ffmpeg engine per command)
nodes.rationale: An isolated engine per op caps peak memory. Its timeout must be duration-scaled, not one-size, because full-timeline re-encodes run at ~0.3× realtime.

nodes.label: The 90s timeout misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Every prior RGB 'abort/OOM/filter bug' was actually runIsolated's hardcoded 90s cap killing a healthy-but-slow encode; ff.terminate() rejected exec with 'called FFmpeg.terminate()' rather than 'timed out', so the catch mis-reported it. Do not chase memory/filter/format theories for RGB compositing again.

nodes.label: Full-frame magenta (lut2 + missing yuv420p conversion)
nodes.rationale: lut2 mishandles packed rgb24 in this wasm build, and leaving the graph output in RGB let the encoder's sws_scale pick a wrong colorspace matrix. Fix: standard blend in planar gbrp plus an explicit format=yuv420p at the END of the chain so the in-graph converter inherits the decode's colorspace metadata.

nodes.label: tpad overlay placement
nodes.rationale: tpad both positions the overlay and gives its stream a frame at t=0; without it the blend framesync buffers every base frame before the start time and OOMs. A setpts-only shift is not a substitute, and -itsoffset stalls framesync.

nodes.label: Do-NOT-re-try list
nodes.rationale: A living record of ruled-out approaches (colorkey/negate fake blends, -itsoffset timing, YUV screen/multiply, unbounded apad + -shortest, music-only mapping, trusting the ffmpeg last-N-lines banner, lut2 in rgb24, one-size timeouts) so failed hypotheses are not re-tried.

nodes.label: EXPORT_QUALITY_PROFILES preset ladder
nodes.rationale: Stepped back to superfast because the blocky-text fix comes from CABAC + deblocking, both ON at superfast; faster/medium bought little visible sharpness on wasm for a big time cost.

nodes.label: MT_ENABLED kill-switch
nodes.rationale: The multi-threaded ffmpeg core is off because it crashed (2 concurrent) then hung (sequential) on the real export filter graph; re-enabling needs real-clip validation and cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP).

nodes.label: Fold localized effects into segment rendering
nodes.rationale: Re-encoding all ~46s just to burn a 3s intro title or a 1–2s fade was the biggest waste; folding titles and fades into per-beat segment graphs eliminates the titled/start_faded/end_faded passes entirely.

nodes.label: probeGoogleFamily
nodes.rationale: Needed because getTitleFontBytes ends in a guaranteed title-sans.ttf fallback, so a typo is otherwise undetectable — it renders in the wrong font instead of failing.

nodes.label: Binding constraint: two seams only
nodes.rationale: The family rides inside the existing fontId as google:Anton so nothing changes shape. No new field on TitleLayerSettings — a sibling field would need adding to the .vidstr package, title presets, the style clipboard and every layer literal, and one missed path is a font that silently reverts on reload.

nodes.label: Hybrid export architecture (WebCodecs + ffmpeg.wasm)
nodes.rationale: WebCodecs handles the pixel-heavy decode→encode path, ffmpeg.wasm keeps the filter graphs, Mediabunny handles mux/demux; feature-detect at runtime so older browsers see zero regression.

nodes.label: Mediabunny (mux/demux/transmux)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over raw mp4-muxer as the maintained successor that handles both mux and demux.

nodes.label: Canvas text rendering over drawtext
nodes.rationale: The browser's own text engine gives proper font shaping, kerning and letter-spacing and matches the CSS preview, eliminating drawtext's tracking, quoting and font-loading issues.

nodes.label: kenBurnsAt(move, t01)
nodes.rationale: One function of time, two uses: it GENERATES the CSS keyframes for playback and is SAMPLED while paused or scrubbing, because a running CSS animation cannot be scrubbed.

nodes.label: kenBurnsChain(w,h,move,durSec)
nodes.rationale: Emits zoompan=d=1 with linear expressions over the frame index and NO scale in the chain. Deltas are computed in TS and emitted as rounded literals because the lerp template produced double-minus expressions like (-8+(8--8)*on/299) for negative focus presets.

nodes.label: kenBurnsVisibleCenter
nodes.rationale: CSS and zoompan disagree about what a focus value means — zoompan's x is the crop's LEFT EDGE within the leftover space, so focus 50 at 2× is centred on 0.75, not 1.0. This is the single source both sides derive from.

nodes.label: coverScale(srcW, srcH, canvasW, canvasH)
nodes.rationale: Fill is computed rather than tabled because the scale that just covers depends on THIS photo's aspect.

nodes.label: zoompan pre-scale spike
nodes.rationale: The spike found a design error, which is why it went first: the in-graph 2× pre-scale ADR-0015 specified was the SLOWEST option, because -loop 1 pushes 300 frames through the graph and scale pays the one-time cost three hundred times. Verdict GO, with the pre-scale moved out of the filter graph into one canvas drawImage. Also found a moving Beat is ~14× the bytes of a static one.

nodes.label: blobUrlCache.ts (permanent Blob URL cache)
nodes.rationale: Module-level, WeakMap-backed cache guaranteeing one stable Blob URL per File/Blob reference so it can never be revoked while a <video> is decoding from it.

nodes.label: Premature Blob URL revocation
nodes.rationale: clipUrlMap built with createObjectURL inside useMemo meant any project-state change fired the effect cleanup and revoked the URL under a live <video>, throwing MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED and rendering a solid black square.

nodes.label: Master clock sync & auto-rewind
nodes.rationale: video.currentTime assignment is asynchronous, so evaluating the out-point on frame 1 of a beat transition read a stale timestamp from the previous beat and froze playback. Pause/step logic now runs against beatElapsed from the performance clock.

nodes.label: buildSegmentGraph (segmentGraph.ts)
nodes.rationale: Makes the Beat filtergraph DATA: four Layer kinds become adapters over one module owning input ordering, index assignment, label naming and who emits [v].

nodes.label: segmentGraph golden master test
nodes.rationale: ~860 lines of exportCut had never had a test, so 'did the refactor change anything?' was answerable only by watching a video. It stands alone: even if nothing follows, any future change to an emitted filter string has to be looked at by a human. Caught a fixture bug — per-Beat titles come from opts.beatTitles keyed by Beat id, not beat.titleLayers.

nodes.label: Second constraint: the base is not a Layer
nodes.rationale: Zoom, Ken Burns, rotation and the Grade stay outside the module. If the interface starts needing 'I am the source' or 'I fork the stream', the boundary is being forced.

nodes.label: SfxSegment / Cut.sfxSegments
nodes.rationale: Modelled on the VO track: filename reference, trim-tail only, volume-only per segment, overlapping SFX allowed.

nodes.label: SFX export mixing (atrim + volume + adelay → amix)
stickerLibrary.ts + /api/stickers
nodes.rationale: Mirrors audioLibrary/sfxLibrary line for line including the basename() traversal guard and the extension allowlist, plus localStorage favourites mirroring voPresets.ts.

nodes.label: stickerCanvas.ts / drawSticker
nodes.rationale: Composes the asset onto a full-frame transparent bitmap at export resolution so preview and export get position/scale/rotation/tint from the same code.

nodes.label: stickerRenderKey
nodes.rationale: Lives next to drawSticker and lists exactly what the renderer reads, so a visual property added later cannot leave the preview's memoised bitmap stale — the bug that made tint appear to do nothing.

nodes.label: resolveSticker
nodes.rationale: Derived at READ time and never written back, so retrimming a Beat can never leave a stale duration behind. It returns a Sticker rather than a separate window type, so every downstream reader needed no change.

nodes.label: fitToBeat (beat-pinned Sticker)
nodes.rationale: Pinning initially over-constrained the chip: a pinned Sticker could not be moved between Beats and a duplicate inherited the pin. Fixed by taking the drag origin from the RESOLVED position and placing a pinned duplicate at the start of the NEXT Beat.

nodes.label: Sticker tint (source-atop)
nodes.rationale: Not a hue slider, because most sticker assets are monochrome icons and rotating the hue of near-black does nothing. Rasterises at the DESTINATION size so a 24×24 SVG does not bake in its own resolution.

nodes.label: Sticker blend mode (added then removed)
nodes.rationale: Removed because blend has no alpha awareness, forcing neutral-colour fills per mode, and because it was the one piece of the feature never verified against a real export. Stickers now composite through alpha with overlay, full stop.

nodes.label: Binding constraint: no drift
nodes.rationale: The library/track half copies the SFX system line for line; the rendering half obeys ADR-0008 so one shared canvas renderer feeds both preview and export.

nodes.label: 'Who emits [v]' exhaustive rule check
nodes.rationale: Re-verified exhaustively across every caption/title/overlay/sticker/rgb combination (162, then 153, then 135) that exactly one stage emits [v] — a failure mode that is otherwise silent.

nodes.label: Clip.kind ("video" | "still")
nodes.rationale: Optional — undefined means video — so saved projects load unchanged.

nodes.label: stillFrame
nodes.rationale: Returns one SampledFrame so posters and the Claude description work from the image itself rather than through a <video>.

nodes.label: beatInputArgs (Still: -loop 1 -t -r 30)
nodes.rationale: Input ORDER is unchanged so the caption/title/overlay/sticker index arithmetic is untouched; a Still's audio always comes from anullsrc.

nodes.label: Binding constraint: no still-specific arithmetic
nodes.rationale: A Still carries a real durationSec of 10, so computeWindow, preBeats, the trimmer and the timeline keep the maths they already have. Only five places branch on Clip.kind.

hyperedges.label: Preview/export parity: one module, two emitters
ffmpeg.wasm export pipeline and its performance/correctness constraints
